text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on October 30. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cholera has broken out in the Zambian capital, claiming two lives and afflicting 24 others since the weekend, medical officials said.
- Counterfeit South African notes are circulating in Zambia, the central bank said. It said the South African Reserve Bank had alerted it that there were 20 Rand notes doing the rounds in Zambia.
- Five 'illegal' miners in the eastern Lundazi district were crushed to death underground when a tunnel they were working in caved in. The miners were digging for gemstones.
- Zambia may have to wait for over three years to benefit from the World Bank and International Monetary fund (IMF) Heavily Indebted Debt Initiative, World Bank officials in Washington said.
- The Zambia Independent Monitoring Team (ZIMT), an election observer group, has accused president Frederick Chiluba of using cash donations to bribe voters ahead of elections on November 18.
